name: Lithium hydroxide monohydrate; production from pre-treated lithium brine; at plant; 100% purity
description:
This unit process produces lithium hydroxide from pre-treated lithium brine using adsorption based direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology. The functional unit of the process is the production of 1 kg of high purity lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LiOH.H20) crystals. The gate-to-gate system boundary starts with the input of pre-treated lithium brine with 57 ppm lithum content and ends with the production high purity LiOH.H2O. The process does not have co-products and all the environmental impacts are allocated to LiOH.H2O production.

Lithium is removed from brine solution using adsroption onto zeolite based adsorbant. Lithium lean brine solution is re-injected back to the brine reservoir. Lithium is then removed using elution with dilute sulfuric acid to generate Li2SO4 solution. Mn, Mg and Ca are removed, reverse osmosis is used to concentrate Li2SO4 solution. Electrodialysis is used to produce LiOH and mechanical vapor compression crystallization to remove excess water and to generate high purity LiOH.H2O. Most water requirements of the process are fullfilled with recycled water and process needs electricity and chemicals for multiple operations. The process generates Mn/Mg/Ca-containing solid waste, which needs to be appropriately disposed. This process was simulated in SysCad simulation tool to generate the mass and energy balances required to calculate the inventory.

processDocumentation.timeDescription: This process was hypothetically designed from up-to-date technologies available for brine lithium extraction. A lab or pilot scale demonstration of the process currently does not exist. Key parameters of the process taken from research papers published in 2022.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: The input brine concentration is based on average Canadian values however, the process may be used in other regions in which the brine concetrations and technologies are similar.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: A zeolite-type absorbent is used to preferentially extract lithium from a pre-treated lithium brine source. Next, the loaded adsorbent is contacted with a dilute sulphuric acid solution to desorb lithium and produce a preconcentrated lithium sulphate stream. The pH of the pre-concentrated lithium sulphate solution is then raised to precipitate dissolved divalent cations, such as Mn, Mg and Ca. After impurities removal, the Li-containing solution is pre-concentrated using Reverse Osmosis (RO) prior to being sent to the Electrodialysis (ED) area where Li2SO4 is split to produce aqueous LiOH and H2SO4 streams. The acidic ED anolyte is recycled upstream to the adsorbent elution stage, whereas the catholyte (LiOH solution) reports to the evaporative crystallization process area to produce LiOH∙H2O monohydrate. Please view the flow diagram below for additional information.
processDocumentation.inventoryMethodDescription: Attributional and gate to gate process.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: The results of this study should be treated according to the AACE Class 5 definition for an engineering study (concept / scoping level). Additional testing is required to validate the process conditions used in this study.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Elementary flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. Technosphere flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. The mass balance for this process was calculated. The model was developed focusing on estimating energy and water consumption. All the key components in input brine solution have been modeled. The datasets is representative in terms of water and soil/solid water emissions. The electrical power consumption estimate is based on major mechanical equipment items only, such as pumps, agitator motors and compressors, but excludes non-process-related electricity consumption (e.g., buildings, site infrastructure, etc.). Land use and transformation impacts are not considered.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Canadian average brine composition is based on field measurements. The process definition and parametes are based on published papers. The results of this study should be treated according to the AACE Class 5 definition for an engineering study (concept / scoping level). Additional testing is required to validate the process conditions used in this study. Ultimately this model serves as a point-estimate in assessing reagent and power consumption for the envisioned process of producing of lithium hydroxide monohydrate from a Li-containing petroleum brine source.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Electricity consumption data all the equipments of the mill is reported as single aggregated value. Granular electricity data can be found in project publication (Kannangara et al. 2024).
processDocumentation.samplingDescription:

Data collection: Data was collected from field measurements, published papers, and process modeling.
Uncertainty: Uncertainty was not evaluated for this process.

reviews.details: Mass balance verified. The developed process flowsheet is based on publicly available information. It should be emphasized, however, that the level of process definition is generally low corresponding to a concept study. Assumptions about process conditions and unit operation performance were often used. These assumptions require validation through laboratory and pilot-scale testing in the future.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication:
SITUATION C1 -- ACCOUNTING The intended application for this process is for accounting purposes as described in Goal Situation C1 from the ILCD Handbook’s Detailed Guidance. LCA studies with this intended application offer "purely descriptive documentation of the system under analysis (e.g., a product, sector or country), without being interested in any potential consequences on other parts of the economy.” The studies categorized under Goal Situation C1 do consider existing benefits outside the analyzed system such as recycling.

The intended application is a purely descriptive accounting / documentation of the analysed system including existing interactions with other systems in the LCI model. The target audience of this model includes LCA practitioners, industry, and the general public.
